title: LCLI-727 follow-ups: the by-hand owner/repo qualifier, derived-name edge cases, the padded-memberId test, and the case-probe controls
description:
Follow-ups from LCLI-727 (F11-F16): the original round-1 review plus the delta review of the correction at 0c1d5737; PR opum-ai/lore-cli#588. All non-blocking. EVERY claim below was MEASURED against the reviewed head before filing, so the line numbers and reproduction outputs are facts rather than relays -- and one of the three original items narrowed to a test gap once measured.

=== FROM THE ROUND-1 REVIEW ===

(1) QUALIFIED-BY-HAND ids skip the predicate. qualifyDecisionRef (src/core/decision-ref.ts:49) never runs its repo part through isValidQualifier, so `--decision opum-ai/lore-cli:DEC-9` is stored verbatim -- an owner/repo PATH, where DEC-192 (5) says the qualifier is the repository NAME only. F11 closed that hole at all three arms that PRODUCE a qualifier (`--repo`, the derived remote name, memberId); this is the fourth path to the same field, where the author supplies it whole. Measured:
    qualifyDecisionRef("opum-ai/lore-cli:DEC-9", "lore-cli")  ->  "opum-ai/lore-cli:DEC-9"   STORED
    qualifyDecisionRef("a b:DEC-9", "lore-cli")               ->  REFUSED ("invalid decision id")
  So the residual hole is `/` and `\`; whitespace cannot reach it, because DECISION_REF's repo part is `[^:\s]+`. FIX: check the repo part with isValidQualifier in qualifyDecisionRef and refuse BY NAME. This conforms to DEC-192 (5) -- the docstring's "kept as authored" rule covers a VALID qualified id, not an owner/repo one. PROVE BOTH WAYS: an owner/repo qualified id is refused by name; a valid `lore-cli:DEC-9` is still stored verbatim; and a bare `DEC-9` still takes its qualifier.

(2) DERIVED-NAME EDGE CASES. repositoryNameFromRemoteUrl (src/core/decision-ref.ts:99) yields a nonsense name from two pre-existing shapes, both confirmed at the reviewed head:
    repositoryNameFromRemoteUrl("https://host:8080")   ->  "8080"     (a PORT is not a repository)
    repositoryNameFromRemoteUrl("https://host:8080/")  ->  "8080"
    repositoryNameFromRemoteUrl("x.git.git")           ->  "x.git"    (the strip takes one suffix)
    repositoryNameFromRemoteUrl("git@host:.git")       ->  undefined  (already safe: empty segment)
  Neither was reachable by F11's tests, which exercised only whitespace and the separators. FIX: pin both with tests AND decide the behaviour in the same change -- the recommendation is to refuse BY NAME a derived name that is numeric-only, or one that came from an empty path segment, rather than writing a port or a truncation into a committed document.

(3) A PADDED memberId IS ALREADY REFUSED -- a TEST gap, not a behaviour gap, measured: resolveDecisionQualifier({ memberId: " lore-cli " }) already throws "invalid workspace member id", while the SAME string passed as --repo trims at src/core/decision-ref.ts:116 and is accepted. That asymmetry is deliberate (memberId is configuration, not a flag, so a padded id would store a padded qualifier) and F11's tests cover the memberId arm's separators but not its padding. FIX: one test pinning that a padded memberId is refused, recording WHY it does not trim where --repo does. No production change.

=== FROM THE DELTA REVIEW OF THE CORRECTION (0c1d5737) ===

(a) THE DECISION-ARM CASE-COLLISION TEST SHOULD ALSO PIN THE SIBLING. It asserts the `--decision` arm returns 0 and that `decisions:` gained the entry, but not that the colliding sibling `adr/0001-a` was left ALONE. The guard it skips is about writing a label that Backlog cannot tell apart from the sibling's; proving the skip should also show the sibling's frontmatter untouched (`decisionsOf("0001-a")` still `[]`). Cheap, and it closes the half of the claim the test does not yet make.

(b) A POSITIVE CONTROL AGAINST A SILENT ALL-SKIP. The case-collision tests are the only real proof of that half, and they are gated on a runtime probe -- so a runner change (a case-INSENSITIVE ubuntu image, or a case-sensitive macOS one) could turn the proof into a GREEN SKIP and nobody would see it. FIX: when the environment says this IS the case-sensitive leg (`process.env.CI` set and `process.platform === "linux"`), assert the probe reported TRUE, failing the suite rather than skipping if it did not. The probe must be able to fail, not only to skip.

(c) COSMETIC: the skip marker says the probe "got one entry back". The probe counts `readdirSync(dir).length === 2`, so the faithful wording is "fewer than two entries" -- a filesystem could in principle return zero, and the message should not name a number it never measured.

=== PREMISE CORRECTED, RECORDED SO IT IS NOT RE-DERIVED ===

One premise of the ROUND-1 review was WRONG and shipped as a test: that the case-collision half is "provably not observable through `link`" because `loadBundle` folds case-colliding ids. It does not -- on a case-sensitive filesystem both concepts load -- and the claim was an artifact of the authoring machine's case-insensitive APFS, where writing `0001-a.md` then `0001-A.md` leaves ONE inode. CI run 38553241722 caught it on the ubuntu leg only. The full account and the rule are on LCLI-727: ON THIS MACHINE, A TEST WHOSE FIXTURE DIFFERS ONLY BY CASE PROVES NOTHING UNTIL A CASE-SENSITIVE FILESYSTEM HAS RUN IT. Item (b) above is what stops that class of error recurring silently.

=== FROM DEC-192 (7) — RATIFIED 2026-10-14 (opum-ai/opum-doc#1020, option A) ===

`superseded_status` is RATIFIED AS BUILT: valid on ANY type, and validated against THAT type's own effective enum. This CLOSES the LCLI-723 review's item (4), which was deliberately left unfiled while opum-doc decided it. The decision is "as built", so no production change follows and neither item below touches behaviour -- one is a test, one is a doc line.

(d) ONE NON-ADR TEST, which is exactly what the ratified shape makes worth proving. Today every proof of `superseded_status` is ADR-only (`[draft, approved]` on an `ADR` type), so the "any type" half of the ruling is unproven. Write it on a NON-ADR type (a `Story` is the natural one) whose own `status` enum lacks `deprecated`, declaring `superseded_status`, and pin all three arms:
    (i)   the profile LOADS with that value;
    (ii)  `lore supersede` WRITES it on a concept of that type;
    (iii) a value OUTSIDE that type's enum is refused AT LOAD, by name.
      A mutation control for (iii): drop the membership check and confirm only (iii) reddens.

(e) THE PROFILE REFERENCE SHOULD SAY "ANY TYPE". The `superseded_status` comment in `DEFAULT_PROFILE_TOML` (src/core/scaffold.ts) sits under an `[[types]]` example, which reads as if the key belonged to one particular type. It should say plainly that it is valid on ANY type and is validated against THAT type's own effective enum. MEASURED so this is not a guess: src/core/scaffold.ts is NOT a declared agent-profile source. The `.lore/agents/*.toml` `sources`/`pinned` lists name lore CONCEPT ids (`reference/cli-surface`, `adr/0005-cli-contract`, `adr/0014-core-has-no-llm-dependency`, …) and never a `src/` path, so this edit grows NO pinned capacity and needs no net-zero accounting. Note the comment already says the value must be a member of "THIS type's `status` enum"; what it does not say is that the key is legal on any type at all, which is the half DEC-192 (7) settles.

plan: 1. Item (1): add the qualifier predicate to qualifyDecisionRef and refuse a hand-supplied owner/repo qualifier by name.
2. Item (2): decide and pin repositoryNameFromRemoteUrl for a numeric-only derived name and the x.git.git truncation.
3. Items (3)(a)(b)(c): tests for the padded memberId, the untouched sibling, the case probe asserted TRUE on the case-sensitive leg, and the skip-marker wording.
4. Item (d): the Story non-ADR superseded_status proofs plus the mutation control.
5. Item (e): the DEFAULT_PROFILE_TOML comment says any type.
6. Gates and delivery: bun run lore check, bun test, typecheck, lint; open the PR; complete the task on the branch.

START HERE FROM THE 2026-10-14 HANDOFF. The outgoing session wrote a full handoff record at LCLI-735 (Session handoff 2026-10-14) - read it before starting, since it carries the campaign state, the residue-cleanup result and two environment traps that will otherwise cost time (bare lore check runs an installed binary that exits 6 on Unrecognized key: targets; the gate is bun run lore check, and /opt/homebrew/bin/bun is not the bare bun).

ON THIS TASK SPECIFICALLY, the outgoing session read the code and CONFIRMED every claim in the description rather than relaying it: qualifyDecisionRef (src/core/decision-ref.ts:49) skips isValidQualifier on its repo part, so --decision opum-ai/lore-cli:DEC-9 is stored verbatim; repositoryNameFromRemoteUrl returns 8080 for https://host:8080 and x.git for x.git.git; the padded-memberId asymmetry is real and deliberate. Tests live in test/link-decision.test.ts.
finalSummary:
Delivered in opum-ai/lore-cli#607, branch fix/LCLI-729-decision-ref-followups.

VALIDATED BY: CI run 38661438218 (pull_request into dev) on commit 7d92a7599b754abadffccd1db9c6a7c0c0afbd9d — 13 jobs success, 1 skipped. The skip is `promotion is manual`, which is SKIPPED BY DESIGN on a PR into dev; that job exists to redden PRs into main. Counting by conclusion: 13 success, 1 skipped, 0 failure. Local gates on the same content: `bun run lore check` 0 (0 errors), `bun test` 5155 pass / 3 skip / 0 fail across 151 files, `tsc --noEmit` 0, `biome check .` 0, plus check:packages, check:lockfile-pins, check:breaking-bump and lint:shell all 0.

ALL EIGHT ITEMS LANDED.

Behaviour fixes. (1) `qualifyDecisionRef` now runs its repo part through `isValidQualifier` and refuses a hand-supplied owner/repo qualifier BY NAME. It was the FOURTH arm writing the stored `<repo>:DEC-N` field — after `--repo`, the derived remote name and the workspace member id — and the only one that skipped the predicate, so `opum-ai/lore-cli:DEC-9` reached a committed document. A valid `<repo>:DEC-N` is still stored verbatim and a bare `DEC-N` still takes the resolved qualifier. (2) `repositoryNameFromRemoteUrl` refuses a NUMERIC-ONLY last segment, so `https://host:8080` no longer yields the port as a repository name; the derived arm returns nothing and the caller answers with its own by-name `--repo` refusal.

DECIDED, NOT CHANGED — the one judgement the task delegated. The single-suffix strip is KEPT, so `x.git.git` yields `x.git`: that is the directory `git clone` itself creates from that URL, so it is the remote own name rather than a truncation this tool invents. `git@host:.git`, which truncates to the empty string, was already refused. Both are now pinned by tests naming the rule.

Tests, with no production change. (3) a padded workspace `memberId` is refused, pinned with the reason it does NOT trim where `--repo` does (a member id is configuration, so a padded one would store a qualifier no reader can match back to the member it names). (a) the doc-side case-collision proof now also asserts the colliding SIBLING was left untouched. (b) on the case-sensitive leg (`CI` set and linux) the runtime case probe is ASSERTED, so the proof fails loudly instead of turning into a green skip. (c) the skip marker says "fewer than two entries", which is what the probe measures. (d) a Story — a NON-ADR type — declaring `superseded_status` with its own `status` enum lacking `deprecated`: the profile loads, `lore supersede` writes the declared value, and an out-of-enum value is refused at load by name. DEC-192 (7) ratified the key as valid on ANY type, and every proof shipped so far was ADR-only. (e) the scaffolded profile reference now says the key is valid on ANY type, validated against THAT type effective enum.

MUTATION CONTROLS, each run on this branch and each reverted cleanly — a passing test that cannot fail is not evidence. The (1) predicate disabled reddens exactly the two new refusal tests. The (2) numeric refusal disabled reddens exactly the two new derived-name tests. The `superseded_status` membership check dropped in `src/core/profile.ts` reddens only (d)(iii). The (b) platform clause removed with `CI=true` on APFS reddens the probe assertion, while the same run without `CI` passes — so it is not vacuous.

LIMIT, STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED. Items (a), (b) and the case-collision pair are gated on a runtime case-sensitivity probe, so they SKIP on this macOS/APFS machine and did not execute here. The ubuntu-latest leg of run 38661438218 is where they actually ran, and it is success.

NO DOCS CONCEPT IS FALSIFIED. `cli-surface.md` describes the BARE id resolution order, which is unchanged. The profile reference edited in (e) lives in the scaffolded `DEFAULT_PROFILE_TOML` (`src/core/scaffold.ts`), not in a pinned docs concept, so no agent-profile capacity moves — `lore check` reports 4 profiles read, 0 over capacity. No CHANGELOG entry was fabricated: `CHANGELOG.md` gains one Fixed entry and one Changed entry under [Unreleased], and check:breaking-bump is green.
